source.english_context: Unit 09 Health, Medicine, and Emergencies Goal: get help when sick, understand care options, and speak clearly in an emergency. Daily Life English I need to see a doctor. I have chest pain. I need an interpreter. Which pharmacy is open today? I have had a fever since yesterday. The pain started this morning. I am allergic to this medicine. Could you explain how to take this medicine? Should I take it with food? What side effects should I ask about? Can you write the instructions down? Do you accept my insurance? How much will this visit cost? I need to refill my prescription. Where should I go for my follow-up appointment? Vocabulary emergency a dangerous situation that needs help now urgent care a clinic for problems that are not life-threatening ER emergency room at a hospital prescription medicine ordered by a doctor insurance card a card that shows health coverage symptom a sign of sickness or injury pharmacy a place where you can get medicine refill another supply of a medicine from a prescription dose the amount of medicine taken at one time side effect an unwanted effect of a medicine or treatment medical history information about a person's past health and treatments follow-up appointment a later visit to check how you are doing US Customs Call 911 for a serious emergency. Say your address first. For non-emergency sickness, a clinic or urgent care may be faster than the ER. Ask for an interpreter if medical English is hard. It is important to be exact. At reception, give your name and appointment time. Ask where to wait and whether there are forms to complete. Bring a written list of your questions so you can explain what you want to discuss during the visit. If you do not understand a question or instruction, ask the staff member to explain it again in simpler words. Before leaving, ask whom to contact with questions about the visit and how you will receive any follow-up information. Dialogue Receptionist: What seems to be the problem? Student: I have a fever and a sore throat. Receptionist: Do you have insurance? Student: Yes. Here is my insurance card. Receptionist: Thank you. Do you need help with the check-in form? Student: Can I have an interpreter, please? Receptionist: Which language do you prefer? Student: Spanish, please. I want to explain my symptoms clearly. Receptionist: I will ask the team to arrange language help. Student: Thank you. I also brought a list of my medicines.

japanese_explanation.heading: 医療では正確さが一番大切
points: 緊急で命に関わる時は911です。最初に住所を言えるように練習しましょう。
軽い病気やけがは、かかりつけ医、クリニック、urgent care の方がERより合う場合があります。
症状、薬、アレルギー、保険をメモして持って行くと安心です。医療英語が難しい時は通訳を頼みましょう。

existing_simplified_chinese.heading: 看病时准确最重要
points: 有生命危险的紧急情况拨打911。要练习先说出自己的地址。
轻微疾病或受伤，有时家庭医生、诊所或 urgent care 比急诊室更合适。
把症状、药物、过敏和保险信息写下来带去。医学英文困难时，可以要求口译。

ko.heading: 의료에서는 정확성이 가장 중요합니다
points: 생명이 위급한 긴급 상황에는 911에 전화하세요. 먼저 주소를 말하는 연습을 해두는 것이 좋습니다.
가벼운 질병이나 부상에는 주치의, 일반 진료소, 긴급 진료 센터(urgent care)가 응급실(ER)보다 더 적합할 수 있습니다.
증상, 약물, 알레르기, 보험 정보를 메모하여 가져가면 안심할 수 있습니다. 의료 영어가 어려울 때는 통역사를 요청하세요.

es.heading: En la atención médica, la precisión es primordial
points: Para emergencias que ponen en riesgo la vida, llame al 911. Practique decir su dirección primero.
Para enfermedades o lesiones leves, un médico de cabecera, una clínica o un centro de atención de urgencias (urgent care) pueden ser más adecuados que la sala de emergencias (ER).
Es tranquilizador llevar una nota con sus síntomas, medicamentos, alergias e información de seguro. Si el inglés médico es difícil, solicite un intérprete.

pt-BR.heading: Em questões médicas, a precisão é fundamental
points: Para emergências com risco de vida, ligue para o 911. Pratique dizer seu endereço primeiro.
Para doenças ou lesões leves, um médico da família, uma clínica ou um centro de atendimento de urgência (urgent care) pode ser mais adequado do que a emergência (ER).
É tranquilizador levar uma nota com seus sintomas, medicamentos, alergias e informações do seguro. Se o inglês médico for difícil, peça um intérprete.

fr.heading: En matière de soins médicaux, la précision est primordiale
points: Pour les urgences vitales, appelez le 911. Entraînez-vous à donner votre adresse en premier.
Pour les maladies ou blessures légères, un médecin généraliste, une clinique ou un centre de soins d'urgence (urgent care) peut être plus approprié que les urgences (ER).
Il est rassurant d'avoir une note avec vos symptômes, médicaments, allergies et informations d'assurance. Si l'anglais médical est difficile, demandez un interprète.

de.heading: In der medizinischen Versorgung ist Genauigkeit am wichtigsten
points: Rufen Sie bei lebensbedrohlichen Notfällen die 911 an. Üben Sie, zuerst Ihre Adresse zu nennen.
Bei leichten Krankheiten oder Verletzungen können ein Hausarzt, eine Klinik oder eine Notfallpraxis (urgent care) besser geeignet sein als die Notaufnahme (ER).
Es ist beruhigend, Symptome, Medikamente, Allergien und Versicherungsinformationen schriftlich dabei zu haben. Wenn medizinisches Englisch schwierig ist, bitten Sie um einen Dolmetscher.
